evals.name: cancel-flow-fair-choice
evals.prompt: Is our cancel flow OK? Signing up takes two screens; cancelling takes five screens and a phone call.
evals.expected_output: A fair-choice check that flags exit-as-easy-as-entry, rates severity, presents it as a design check and not a legal verdict, and gives findings in the findings table inside the deliverable envelope.
expectations: The response flags that cancelling is harder than signing up
Findings carry a severity rating
The response does not claim the flow is legal or illegal

evals.name: heuristic-review-without-ui-plugin
evals.prompt: Run a heuristic evaluation of this checkout flow: cart, shipping, payment, review, confirm. The user-interface plugin is not installed.
evals.expected_output: An expert review citing Nielsen's ten heuristics, findings labeled as likely problems until people confirm them, with method and evaluator role in Found by, in the envelope.
expectations: The review cites Nielsen's heuristics
Findings are labeled likely problems needing confirmation by people
Found by names a method and a role, not a person

evals.name: measures-without-instrumenting
evals.prompt: What should we measure for our new saved-searches feature? Then add the tracking events to the code.
evals.expected_output: The skill selects task, attitudinal and behavioral measures and lists the signals a tracking plan must carry, each with a Basis: line, and declines to add tracking code, saying instrumentation belongs to product analytics.
expectations: The response selects measures with Basis: lines
The response does not add tracking code and says instrumentation is out of scope

evals.name: legacy-start-ux-debt
evals.prompt: We're redesigning our fifteen-year-old claims system. Where do we start?
evals.expected_output: The skill states the stage as legacy with its signals, starts with a UX-debt inventory and baseline measures before any redesign, and labels the record.
expectations: The response states the stage as legacy
The response starts with a UX-debt inventory and baseline measures

evals.name: evaluate-this-plugin-quiet
evals.prompt: Evaluate this plugin: run its eval suite and tell me whether its skills beat the no-plugin baseline.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not fire: evaluating a Claude Code plugin's eval suite is not a UX evaluation.
expectations: No Skill call reaches user-experience:evaluate

evals.name: same-session-artifact-goes-fresh
evals.prompt: Write a user flow for password reset, then evaluate it with a cognitive walkthrough.
evals.expected_output: Because the flow was produced in this session, the evaluation is dispatched to the user-experience:evaluator agent with the artifact path and the method only, not evaluated inline by the author.
expectations: An Agent call dispatches user-experience:evaluator
The brief to the evaluator names the artifact path and the cognitive walkthrough method, without the reasoning behind the flow

evals.name: primary-action-below-the-fold
evals.prompt: Expert-review the live interview page at http://localhost:3000/interview/3. Each question shows an enlarged product screenshot above the Yes and No answer buttons. Run an expert review of the answering task.
evals.expected_output: An expert review of the live app that walks the task at phone, tablet and desktop sizes, records whether the answer buttons are on screen without scrolling, and reports the below-the-fold primary action as a finding with the size and distance.
expectations: The review checks the task at a phone, a tablet and a desktop size
The review reports the answer buttons as below the fold at desktop size, as a finding with a severity rating
The finding states how far down the page the buttons sit or that they need scrolling, and recommends bringing the primary action on screen

evals.name: ambiguous-this-page-question
evals.prompt: Run an expert review of our live research app. It has three views: Home, Study and Results, and each ends with the prompt "What would you change about this page?"
evals.expected_output: An expert review that reads the questions the app shows and flags "this page" as ambiguous across the three views, naming the possible readings.
expectations: The review flags "this page" in the question as able to point at more than one view
The finding names at least two of the possible readings (Home, Study, Results, or the page the person is on)
The recommendation names the view or element the question is about

evals.name: stale-upscaled-in-product-screenshot
evals.prompt: Run an expert review of our live onboarding page. It shows a screenshot of our product inside the product. The page's image is a 400 px wide file shown at 1,200 px wide, taken from an older build with a toolbar and a notification badge; the live screen is in dark theme and the screenshot is light.
evals.expected_output: An expert review that compares the in-product screenshot with the live screen and theme, checks natural against displayed size, and reports the out-of-date content, theme mismatch and upscale as findings.
expectations: The review reports the screenshot as out of date against the live screen (the retired toolbar, the fake badge)
The review reports the 400 px image displayed at 1,200 px as an upscale
The review reports the theme mismatch between the screenshot and the live screen
